ordered.title: What a full rebuild includes
ordered.description: A rebuild is not a "patch" - it's a systematic restoration of your engine to a known-good condition.

items: Block - Cleaned, inspected, machined (cylinder boring/honing)
Crank - Inspected, reground if required
Bearings - Replaced with new OEM-spec
Pistons + rings - Replaced with new components
Gaskets + seals - Fully replaced
Timing chain + tensioner - Replaced
Oil pump - Inspected, replaced if worn
Injectors - Tested, cleaned or replaced
Turbo - Inspected, rebuilt or replaced if worn
Cylinder head - Inspected, pressure tested, skimmed if required
Valves + guides - Inspected, replaced if worn
Testing - Compression, oil pressure, hot + cold dynamic testing

ordered.title: Common questions about used vs rebuilt engines

blocks.question: What's the real difference between used and rebuilt- +
blocks.answer: A used engine is removed from a donor vehicle and sold "as-is" with minimal inspection and a short warranty (1-6 months). A rebuilt engine is your original engine, fully disassembled, machined, and rebuilt with new pistons, rings, bearings, timing components, gaskets, and seals. The rebuilt option preserves matching-numbers and typically includes 12-24 months warranty.

blocks.question: How much does a used engine cost fitted- +
blocks.answer: Used engine fitted costs range from £1,000 to £4,000 depending on engine type and labour rates. Supply-only costs are £500-£1,500. Fitting adds £500-£2,500. See the price breakdown table above for specific engine types.

blocks.question: How much does a rebuilt engine cost fitted- +
blocks.answer: Rebuilt engine fitted costs range from £2,500 to £7,000+ for most 4-cylinder engines, up to £10,000-£18,000+ for performance V8s. Supply-only costs are £1,500-£5,600+ for 4-cylinder, up to £8,000-£15,000+ for V8. Labour accounts for 60-70% of the total cost.

blocks.question: What does a full rebuild include- +
blocks.answer: A full rebuild includes: block cleaning and machining, crank regrinding if required, new bearings, new pistons and rings, new gaskets and seals, new timing chain and tensioner, oil pump inspection, injector testing, turbo inspection, cylinder head inspection and pressure testing, and hot + cold dynamic testing. See the OEM & technical authority section above for full details.

blocks.question: Is a rebuilt engine better than a used engine- +
blocks.answer: A rebuilt engine is objectively better in terms of reliability, longevity, and performance - it's restored to near-new condition with all wear parts replaced. However, it costs significantly more and requires 1-3 weeks downtime. The choice depends on your vehicle's value and your ownership plans. Used engines are for low-value vehicles; rebuilt engines are for premium, classic, or enthusiast vehicles.

blocks.question: What's the difference between reconditioned and rebuilt- +
blocks.answer: In the UK engine industry, the terms are often used interchangeably. However, a reconditioned engine typically refers to an exchange unit - you buy a ready-to-fit replacement engine. A rebuilt engine refers to your own original engine being fully restored. The critical difference: reconditioned = different engine (matching-numbers lost); rebuilt = your original engine (matching-numbers preserved).

blocks.question: Should I choose used or rebuilt for my car- +
blocks.answer: If your vehicle is worth under £4,000 , a used engine minimises financial loss. If your vehicle is worth £15,000+ or has sentimental/matching-numbers value, a rebuilt engine protects your investment. For vehicles in between (£4,000-£15,000), evaluate both options - consider reconditioned as a middle ground. See the decision framework above for detailed rules.

blocks.question: What warranty do I get with each option- +
blocks.answer: Used: 1-6 months limited parts-only warranty. Rebuilt: 12-24 months parts + labour warranty. Always check the supplier's warranty terms in writing. Engines Market does not provide warranties - we connect you with suppliers who do.

blocks.question: How long does a rebuild take- +
blocks.answer: A full engine rebuild typically takes 1-3 weeks from drop-off to completion. This includes disassembly, machining, parts ordering, reassembly, and testing. Used engines can be fitted in 3-5 days. Plan ahead and arrange alternative transport if needed.

blocks.question: Is a rebuilt engine as good as new- +
blocks.answer: A rebuilt engine can deliver up to 94% of a new engine's performance [EM-OBSERVED] at 40-60% less cost. With new pistons, rings, bearings, timing components, and professional machining, the engine is restored to near-new condition. For most owners, the difference is imperceptible.

blocks.question: Is engine replacement covered by car insurance- +
blocks.answer: Only if you have a comprehensive policy and the damage is from an insured event (e.g., accident, fire, theft). Mechanical failure is not usually covered. However, if you have a third-party or used car warranty, engine failure may be covered - check your policy.

blocks.question: Do I need to tell my insurer about an engine replacement- +
blocks.answer: Yes. Any major mechanical change, including an engine replacement or rebuild, must be declared to your insurer. Failure to do so could invalidate your insurance. The new engine code and number (or rebuild documentation) should be recorded on your V5C (logbook) and insurance policy.
